label: Development robustness screen — revealed synthetic reference
freeze_statement: This protocol, perturbation values, evaluation rules and numerical settings were saved before the first v0.2 stress evaluation. H1/H2 and all v0.1 outcomes were already revealed. No independent-validation claim is made.
selection_policy: Select the priority queue from the planning ensemble before this audit. Replay it unchanged. Never rank, repair or replace it using stress outcomes. A user may explicitly audit another pre-existing queue, recorded as a development assessment.
reference_policy: Same-scenario no additional discretionary work from the identical verified starting state; the same work deadline and return reserve apply.
screened_states: Every achieved completed-work prefix and the final state from the shared causal replay, at every declared protected node.
passing_rule: All selected planning cases and every required development case resolve and pass the common protected-node spill gate. Any missing/numerically invalid result is unresolved; a valid harmful prefix or final state fails. No averaging away failures.
epsilon_policy: Use the unchanged case epsilon_m3 (0.05 m3 in the reference case) and the planner's 1e-9 m3 comparison allowance. Do not enlarge epsilon after outcomes.

numerical_settings.rule: Every baseline and achieved prefix/final state must have valid default, half-step and extended-horizon engine runs with matching model, forcing and engine. Require per-node spill convergence within max(0.05 m3, 2% of the larger absolute default/half-step magnitude), extra spill within 0.05 m3 per protected node and total by 360 minutes, and identical protected-node pass/fail at both routing steps. Any missing check, failure or classification flip is unresolved.

parameter_design: Two-sided flow and roughness sensitivities; one-sided tighter current restrictions; less available storage; elevated receiving stage; existing maximum job times; one interaction corner. This compact deterministic design is neither exhaustive nor probabilistic and was not optimized for a favourable queue.

limitations: All cases use the same synthetic catchment. H1/H2 have already been revealed; no independent validation or field effectiveness is established.
The parameter values are illustrative engineering sensitivities, not calibrated uncertainty bounds, probabilities or return periods.
Spill is removed at named drainage-model boundaries. It is not mapped street flooding, damage or crew safety.
The hydraulic experiment starts cold. Horizon-sensitive cases fail numerical adequacy; agreement by 360 minutes does not establish field-valid antecedent conditions.
Engine validity, step-halving, doubled-horizon and protected-decision checks are mandatory for each achieved state. Numerical agreement is software evidence, not physical calibration.
Passing this finite set does not guarantee non-worsening between or beyond its members, under wet work, or on another catchment.
Hashes detect stale or altered local evidence; they are not a digital signature, role authentication or independent laboratory attestation.
pre_evaluation_amendment: Before any v0.2 evaluation, numerical adequacy was strengthened to require step halving, a doubled horizon and stable protected-node decisions. The symmetric convergence scale is identical to the existing numerical verification. No hydraulic stress outcome had been computed or inspected.
